key_insight: A genome-guided, physics-informed screening pipeline can rapidly narrow a huge lead-free double-perovskite design space to a handful of phase-stable, optoelectronically promising absorbers with DFT-validated design rules.
engineering_relevance: The study provides interpretable screening rules for discovering stable, lead-free semiconductor materials for solar cells, sensors, and transparent electronics without relying on trial-and-error synthesis.
method: Train surrogate models on 1,221 DFT-calculated A2BB'X6 compounds using four descriptor families: packing, bonding, polarization, and electronic identity.
Use a recall-optimized stability classifier and XGBoost band-gap regressor to rank 13,088 charge-balanced compositions.
Apply staged inverse-design constraints and validate the top candidates with DFT and convex-hull analysis.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong model performance (ROC-AUC = 0.92 for stability, R2 = 0.93 for band-gap prediction) and identifies five DFT-validated compounds on or at the convex hull with strong absorption (~10^5 cm^-1).
watch_item: The pipeline is trained on DFT data and candidate discovery still depends on computational labels, so experimental synthesis stability and defect tolerance remain to be confirmed.
paper_title: Genome-Guided Interpretable Screening of Phase-Stable, Lead-Free Double Perovskite Absorbers for All-Inorganic Semiconductors, Sensors, and Photovoltaics with DFT-Validated Design Rules
